text: “m/w/d” is an abbreviation of “männlich, weiblich oder divers”. This guide explains why it appears on German job listings.

German job offers often show “m/w/d” in the title. It’s an abbreviation for “männlich, weiblich oder divers” – “male, female or diverse”. This abbreviation means that the job offer is open to all genders, even if the job title is masculine.

title: Alternative abbreviations
text: The abbreviation is sometimes in a different order, like “d/w/m”, to avoid putting men first and diverse people last. Other letters like “a” (other), “t” (transsexual), “i” (intersexual), “gn” (gender neutral) and “x” (undefined) are sometimes used.

Hiring discrimination based on gender is illegal. Companies add this information in their job offers to prevent discrimination lawsuits.
